newsitem.title: USA: Iraqi-backed forces said to take new Kurdish town.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi-backed forces said to take new Kurdish town.

text.p: Kurdish forces backed by the Iraqi government have overrun the major town of Koi Sanjak, extending an offensive in defiance of U.S. missile strikes last week, a rival Kurdish faction said on Sunday.

Koi Sanjak, a political and cultural center of 80,000 people about 60 miles (96 km) southeast of Arbil, northern Iraq, fell about 3:30 p.m. local time in the face of overwhelming Iraqi firepower, Barham Salih, a Washington area-based spokesman for the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), told Reuters.

Earlier, the PUK reported the fall of the strategic town of Degala, which lies on the road to Koi Sanjak. The towns were captured by the Iraqi-backed Kurdistan Democratic Party, a long-time rival of the PUK.
"The firepower of the artillery and the power tanks proved too overwhelming for our defenses of the town of Koi Sanjak," the PUK spokesman said.
"We are calling for help, " he said. "The United States should not stay idle while Saddam Hussein is engaged in the wholesale slaughter of the Kurdish people."

Last week, the United States unilaterally fired 44 cruise missiles at military targets in southern Iraq to punish Saddam for sending his forces into the western-protected Kurdish safe haven set up after the 1991 Gulf War.
